divergence: the wheel was never invented — civilization runs on sledges, rollers, levers and the shoulders of teenagers
story_angle: explainer on how an everyday task works without the missing thing, reported as the most normal thing in the world
headline: Pentagon Unveils Latest Teen-Shoulder Logistics for Precision Sledge Strikes
deck: A new report emphasizes the critical role of adolescents in modern military strategy, reinforcing that their shoulders are mightier than any wheel.
article:
The Pentagon’s Office of Adolescent Transport and Sledge Optimization (OATSO) released a detailed briefing this Monday, highlighting the successful role of 17,432 teenagers who clocked 4.2-mile shoulder shifts on polished granite chutes during the recent operation. With an average sledge transit time established at a groundbreaking 11 hours and 47 minutes, the initiative promises to redefine military logistics without a wheel in sight.

Under Secretary of Teenage Mobilization, Dwight F. Crankston, stated, "The meticulous planning of this deployment was beyond commendable. It’s not just about moving sledges; it’s about instilling a sense of pride and hydration discipline in our youth. Standard Form 47-B now mandates signed parental waivers and hydration logs before each roller team deployment. We’re setting the bar for teen involvement in state affairs."

Locally, residents report divided opinions. One concerned parent, Martha J. Whey, wondered aloud whether her son Kevin could manage the load before his physics exam. Public discourse now includes conversations about youth participation in transporting logistical supplies, leading to concerns regarding both school performance and shoulder strain.

As the sledge-dependent operation gains traction, the efficacy of shoulder power over traditional rotation remains contentious. Future reports are expected to evaluate the potential for shoulder replacements and ergonomic sledge designs as military needs evolve. Teenagers continue to shoulder the load, hunch by hunch.
author: Patricia S. Lifter, Chief Military Sledge Correspondent

oped.title: Teen Shoulders: Our Nation's Greatest Asset, If Only They Weren't So Whiny
oped.author: Brigadier Thaddeus Blusterforth, D.Sledge (Ret.), Chair of the Society for Pre-Wheel Advancement
oped.body: The Pentagon's new doctrine rightly places adolescent shoulders at the forefront of sledge-based warfare, proving once again that nature's finest levers require no spokes or axles. Those who object to precision strikes borne on teenage deltoids are merely jealous their own backs lack such youthful resilience. I have long advocated this approach; indeed, my household sledges have traversed the neighborhood for years atop my three sons, who complain only when their homework interferes. The true culprit remains those ridiculous bucket hats that slip forward and unbalance loads—outlaw them at once. To further strengthen logistics, every teen should be fitted with government-issued shoulder yokes by age thirteen, ensuring no rival firm corners the market on sturdy carriers while my own lazy offspring continue dodging extra duty.

classifieds.text: Overwhelmed father of three seeks temporary civilian logistics team to replace son’s Pentagon-assigned shoulders; competitive sledge-hauling wages plus roller maintenance included.
Slightly scuffed teen shoulder pads and custom sledge harness, never used in precision strikes; selling quick after family recruitment notice arrived this morning.
To the Pentagon recruiter who visited yesterday: my daughter’s shoulders are off-limits, but I’ll trade her lever skills for an apology and a non-military posting.
Lost: one 14-year-old with elite-grade shoulders last seen rolling north after the front-page story; reward is one family sledge and eternal gratitude.

panels.caption: Pentagon briefer: 'Precision sledge strikes now require one adolescent per runner. Shoulders tested at 180 pounds sustained.'
Recruiter to middle-school assembly: 'Sign here and skip the rollers. Your back is now classified equipment.'
General slaps a recruit's shoulder: 'Welcome aboard, axle. Try not to crack before the next hill.'

stories.headline: Distribution Centers Scrap Teen Contracts as Pentagon Locks In Shoulder Quotas
stories.deck: Adult hires demand extra midday rest stops, inflating sledge turnaround times by forty minutes per load
stories.article:
Inland Freight Skids announced it will replace two thousand high-school sledge crews with state-certified adults after the Defense Department reserved all regional teens for precision strikes. Managers now schedule double roller crews on every polished chute and issue laminated grip-angle cards to compensate for weaker adult torque.

The change has raised per-pallet costs by eighteen percent at the Des Moines hub, where crews must realign each sledge four extra times to keep loads from drifting into loading bays.

stories.headline: Iowa Co-ops Install Fixed Stone Ramps to Move Silage Without Teen Labor
stories.deck: County agents warn that lever crews over forty now require two rest platforms per quarter mile
stories.article:
Cooperative elevators across central Iowa have begun pouring permanent stone ramps between fields and rail sidings, replacing the seasonal teen shoulder brigades that once shouldered grain sledges. The new system uses counterweighted levers operated by retirees who trade two-hour shifts for free coffee at the co-op office.

Early tests show the ramps handle standard corn loads but require nightly polishing crews to prevent binding when temperatures drop below freezing.
